    <h2>How do I make a donation to Creative Commons?</h2>
<p>We offer many ways to donate. We invite you to use <a href="https://giving.gofundme.com/campaign/778218/donate">our secure and encrypted online donation form</a> hosted by GoFundMe Pro (formerly known as Classy). GoFundMe Pro supports payments by credit card, ACH, digital wallets, and cryptocurrency, including Apple Pay, Microsoft Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Venmo, and Coinbase.</p>
<p>You can also make a donation via check. Please make your check payable to “Creative Commons,” and mail to our address below:</p>
<p>Creative Commons<br />
PO Box 741107<br />
Los Angeles CA 90074-1107</p>
<h2>I’d like to become a monthly donor. How do I do this?</h2>
<p><a href="https://giving.gofundme.com/campaign/778218/donate">Visit our secure and encrypted online donation page</a> hosted by GoFundMe Pro to set up a monthly contribution. GoFundMe Pro supports payments by credit card, ACH, digital wallets, and cryptocurrency, including Apple Pay, Microsoft Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Venmo, and Coinbase.</p>
<h2>I’m already a monthly donor. How can I adjust, update or cancel my donation?</h2>
<p>You can manage your recurring donation on our fundraising platform, GoFundMe Pro. <a href="https://support.classy.org/s/article/how-to-edit-a-recurring-donation">Click here for detailed information</a> on how to edit or cancel your monthly donation.</p>
<h2>Are donations tax-deductible?</h2>
<p>Creative Commons Corporation is a 501(c)3 tax-exempt organization and your donation is tax-deductible within the guidelines of U.S. law. To claim a donation as a deduction on your U.S. taxes, please keep your email donation receipt as your official record. We’ll always send it your way upon successful completion of your donation.</p>
<h2>What is your federal employment identification number?</h2>
<p>Our federal employment identification number (FEIN) is 04-3585301.</p>
<h2>Do you accept donations through PayPal?</h2>
<p>Yes, we do! You can <a href="https://www.paypal.com/donate/?hosted_button_id=RHB7C3BUX9646" target="_blank" rel="noopener">make a donation to Creative Commons through PayPal here</a>.</p>
<h2>I would like to make a wire transfer donation to Creative Commons. How do I do this?</h2>
<p>If you would like to make a gift via wire transfer, please contact <a href="mailto:development@creativecommons.org">development@creativecommons.org</a>.</p>
<h2>I’d like to add Creative Commons to my will. How do I do this?</h2>
<p>Creative Commons does not currently have a planned giving program. If you would like to make a lasting impact by including us in your will, we suggest you visit <a href="https://www.freewill.com/">FreeWill</a> or consult an attorney or estate planning professional. You can also check out <a href="https://www.fidelitycharitable.org/guidance/philanthropy/what-are-bequests.html">this useful resource from Fidelity Charitable on bequests</a> and how to include nonprofits in your will or trust.</p>
<h2>Do you accept gifts via stocks or securities?</h2>
<p>Yes, we do. To make a gift via stock or securities, please contact <a href="mailto:development@creativecommons.org">development@creativecommons.org</a> for account information.</p>
<h2>Do you accept gifts via donor advised funds (DAF)?</h2>
<p>Yes, we do. You may send DAF donations through <a href="https://www.dafdirect.org/DAFDirect/daflink?_dafdirect_settings=MDQzNTg1MzAxXzIxMTFfN2UzNjQyM2QtNzQ2OS00MmQyLWJiMmEtOWM2YmI2NzJiY2U2&designatedText=&amountValue=">DAF Direct</a>, or you can reach out to <a href="mailto:development@creativecommons.org">development@creativecommons.org</a> for other options.</p>
<h2>Do you accept employer matching donations?</h2>
<p>Yes, we do. Matching gifts are a great way to double your impact. We encourage you to check in with your employer about the matching programs available at your company. If you do move forward with an employer match, please let us know at <a href="mailto:development@creativecommons.org">development@creativecommons.org</a>.</p>
<h2>Do you accept cryptocurrency?</h2>
<p>Yes. We currently accept donations of cryptocurrency on <a href="https://giving.gofundme.com/campaign/778218/donate">GoFundMe Pro</a> (via Coinbase), <a href="https://www.every.org/creative-commons">Every</a> and <a href="https://app.endaoment.org/orgs/043585301">Endaoment</a>.</p>
<h2>I’ve heard you sell Creative Commons merchandise. Where can I buy some?</h2>
<p>Yes, we offer Creative Commons merchandise!  Check out <a href="http://creative-commons-shop.fourthwall.com/">our store</a> for CC-branded merch.</p>
<h2>Are there other ways to support CC besides donating money?</h2>
<p>There are many ways to get involved with Creative Commons. We encourage you to <a href="https://mail.creativecommons.org/subscribe">sign up for our newsletter</a>, check out our <a href="https://creativecommons.org/blog/">blog</a> and visit our <a href="https://twitter.com/creativecommons">Twitter</a>, <a href="https://www.facebook.com/creativecommons">Facebook</a>, <a href="https://www.instagram.com/creativecommons/">Instagram</a>, <a href="https://mastodon.social/@creativecommons">Mastodon</a>, and <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/creative-commons">LinkedIn</a> pages. We always appreciate our supporters who spread the word about our work!</p>
<h2>Other questions?</h2>
<p>If you have any other donation related questions, please don’t hesitate to reach to <a href="mailto:development@creativecommons.org">development@creativecommons.org</a>.</p>

Open Infrastructure Circle Donor FAQ CC Contributions Policy CC Guidelines for Screening Donors US State Nonprofit Disclosures How do I make a donation to Creative Commons? We offer many ways to donate. We invite you to use our secure and encrypted online donation form hosted by GoFundMe Pro (formerly known as Classy). GoFundMe Pro supports payments by credit card, ACH, digital wallets, and cryptocurrency, including Apple Pay, Microsoft Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Venmo, and Coinbase. You can also make a donation via check. Please make your check payable to “Creative Commons,” and mail to our address below: Creative Commons PO Box 741107 Los Angeles CA 90074-1107 I’d like to become a monthly donor. How do I do this? Visit our secure and encrypted online donation page hosted by GoFundMe Pro to set up a monthly contribution. GoFundMe Pro supports payments by credit card, ACH, digital wallets, and cryptocurrency, including Apple Pay, Microsoft Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Venmo, and Coinbase. I’m already a monthly donor. How can I adjust, update or cancel my donation? You can manage your recurring donation on our fundraising platform, GoFundMe Pro. Click here for detailed information on how to edit or cancel your monthly donation. Are donations tax-deductible? Creative Commons Corporation is a 501(c)3 tax-exempt organization and your donation is tax-deductible within the guidelines of U.S. law. To claim a donation as a deduction on your U.S. taxes, please keep your email donation receipt as your official record. We’ll always send it your way upon successful completion of your donation. What is your federal employment identification number? Our federal employment identification number (FEIN) is 04-3585301. Do you accept donations through PayPal? Yes, we do! You can make a donation to Creative Commons through PayPal here . I would like to make a wire transfer donation to Creative Commons. How do I do this? If you would like to make a gift via wire transfer, please contact development@creativecommons.org . I’d like to add Creative Commons to my will. How do I do this? Creative Commons does not currently have a planned giving program. If you would like to make a lasting impact by including us in your will, we suggest you visit FreeWill or consult an attorney or estate planning professional. You can also check out this useful resource from Fidelity Charitable on bequests and how to include nonprofits in your will or trust. Do you accept gifts via stocks or securities? Yes, we do. To make a gift via stock or securities, please contact development@creativecommons.org for account information. Do you accept gifts via donor advised funds (DAF)? Yes, we do. You may send DAF donations through DAF Direct , or you can reach out to development@creativecommons.org for other options. Do you accept employer matching donations? Yes, we do. Matching gifts are a great way to double your impact. We encourage you to check in with your employer about the matching programs available at your company. If you do move forward with an employer match, please let us know at development@creativecommons.org . Do you accept cryptocurrency? Yes. We currently accept donations of cryptocurrency on GoFundMe Pro (via Coinbase), Every and Endaoment . I’ve heard you sell Creative Commons merchandise. Where can I buy some? Yes, we offer Creative Commons merchandise! Check out our store for CC-branded merch. Are there other ways to support CC besides donating money? There are many ways to get involved with Creative Commons. We encourage you to sign up for our newsletter , check out our blog and visit our Twitter , Facebook , Instagram , Mastodon , and LinkedIn pages. We always appreciate our supporters who spread the word about our work! Other questions? If you have any other donation related questions, please don’t hesitate to reach to development@creativecommons.org . Get the latest CC news, updates, events, resources, and more right to your inbox! <h2>Goal 1: Strengthen the open infrastructure of sharing</h2>
<p>We imagine a world where CC’s foundational open infrastructure is funded by default, and where individual creators and rightsholders reclaim agency in contributing to and benefiting from the commons. If we can ensure a strong and resilient open infrastructure of sharing that enables access to educational resources, cultural heritage, and scientific research in the public interest, we’ll have a viable alternative to the concentrations of power that currently exist and aim to restrict sharing and access. Because the commons must continue to exist for everyone. We cannot allow an undesirable future to emerge unchallenged.</p>
<h2>Goal 2: Defend and advocate for a thriving creative commons</h2>
<p>Stronger open infrastructure enables the thriving creative commons that is required to solve the world’s greatest problems. Knowledge must be accessible, discoverable, and reusable. In tandem with a strong and supported open infrastructure of sharing, a thriving creative commons redistributes power from the hands of the few to the minds of the many, and cements a worldview of knowledge as a public good and a human right. It’s time for new approaches that tell the stories of how we can all benefit from the commons, and for an increase of reciprocal sharing of the knowledge that will advance solutions to the greatest problems of our time.</p>
<h2>Goal 3: Center community</h2>
<p>Community is not a means to an end. It is central to everything we do and at the heart of our mission and vision. We aim to better center the community of open advocates, who are credited for the global usability and adoption of the CC legal tools, alongside the rich generational and geographical diversity of open advocates with varying needs and awareness of CC. It is not only open advocates who benefit from the commons or who need clarity on how their work is being used with emerging technologies. It is everyone who benefits or contributes, whether they consider themselves part of the movement or not.</p>

Goal 1: Strengthen the open infrastructure of sharing We imagine a world where CC’s foundational open infrastructure is funded by default, and where individual creators and rightsholders reclaim agency in contributing to and benefiting from the commons. If we can ensure a strong and resilient open infrastructure of sharing that enables access to educational resources, cultural heritage, and scientific research in the public interest, we’ll have a viable alternative to the concentrations of power that currently exist and aim to restrict sharing and access. Because the commons must continue to exist for everyone. We cannot allow an undesirable future to emerge unchallenged. Goal 2: Defend and advocate for a thriving creative commons Stronger open infrastructure enables the thriving creative commons that is required to solve the world’s greatest problems. Knowledge must be accessible, discoverable, and reusable. In tandem with a strong and supported open infrastructure of sharing, a thriving creative commons redistributes power from the hands of the few to the minds of the many, and cements a worldview of knowledge as a public good and a human right. It’s time for new approaches that tell the stories of how we can all benefit from the commons, and for an increase of reciprocal sharing of the knowledge that will advance solutions to the greatest problems of our time. Goal 3: Center community Community is not a means to an end. It is central to everything we do and at the heart of our mission and vision. We aim to better center the community of open advocates, who are credited for the global usability and adoption of the CC legal tools, alongside the rich generational and geographical diversity of open advocates with varying needs and awareness of CC. It is not only open advocates who benefit from the commons or who need clarity on how their work is being used with emerging technologies. It is everyone who benefits or contributes, whether they consider themselves part of the movement or not.
